cards.text: Friend, things got heavy in Numbers 14. The LORD said everyone twenty and older who grumbled will fall in the wilderness, and their children will enter the land, along with Caleb and Joshua, two of the men who spied it out (Numbers 14:29-31, 38). Now the LORD speaks to Moses, Israel's leader.

cards.question: The LORD's new message for the Israelites starts by saying when these instructions kick in. When is it?

answers.text: After they enter the land He's giving them
While they wander in the wilderness
Once the forty years are halfway done

cards.text: Not if, friend. AFTER. Then He lays out what comes with an animal offering from the herd or flock, whether for a vow, a freewill offering or an appointed feast: fine flour mixed with olive oil, plus wine as a drink offering. A lamb gets the least, a ram gets more, a young bull gets the most, and every animal gets its portion, no matter how many. Every amount spelled out, and I've been eyeballing sprinkles my whole life.
Every native-born Israelite does it this way. And a foreigner living among them might want to bring a food offering to the LORD too.

cards.question: If a foreigner living among the Israelites wants to bring a food offering to the LORD, how does he do it?

answers.text: With half the flour and oil

cards.question: The LORD says the native-born and the foreigner have one law, and it's a ___ statute.

cards.text: Then the LORD gives Moses another message for the Israelites. When they enter the land and eat its food, they're to lift up an offering to the LORD.

cards.question: When the Israelites eat the food of the land, the LORD wants an offering from the first of something. What is it?

answers.text: The first of their olive oil

cards.text: DOUGH, friend. A stamper hears that word and his whole handle lights up. They lift up a cake from the first of it as a contribution, just like an offering from the threshing floor.

cards.question: True or false: The offering from the first of the dough is a one-time gift for their first harvest in the land.

cards.text: Now the LORD turns to something new for Moses to pass along. What if they stray unintentionally and don't obey all the commands He's given through Moses, from the first day on down the generations?
You know, like setting the oven timer and never hitting start. And say the whole congregation slips up like that, without even knowing it.

cards.question: When the whole congregation sins unintentionally, what do they bring to the LORD?

answers.text: One young bull and one male goat
Two lambs and a pair of doves

cards.question: The priest makes atonement for the whole congregation, and because the sin was unintentional, they will be ___.
True or false: The foreigners living among the Israelites are forgiven right along with them.

cards.text: Now say just one person sins unintentionally. Friend, I know that one: I live alone in my bakery, so every upside-down cookie is a mystery with ONE suspect.

cards.question: When one person sins unintentionally, what does he bring as a sin offering?

answers.text: A young bull from the herd

cards.text: The priest makes atonement before the LORD for that person, and once it's done, he's forgiven. One mistake, one goat, one clean slate.

cards.question: True or false: For one person's unintentional sin, a foreigner living among the Israelites follows a different law than a native-born Israelite.

cards.text: But now the LORD draws a line. This isn't about straying by accident. It's about the person who sins defiantly, whether he's a native or a foreigner.

cards.question: The LORD says the person who sins defiantly is doing something against Him. What is it?
True or false: The person who sins defiantly is forgiven, just like the one who sinned unintentionally.
The LORD says the person who sins defiantly will certainly be cut off from his people. Why?

answers.text: He despised the word of the LORD
He defiled the camp of the LORD
He neglected the feasts of the LORD
